title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: S is a base scheme. Here it is of finite type over Q and assumed to be an algebraic K(pi,1). X -> S is a relative (smooth) curve and U is X minus some disjoint sections (marked points / cusps). E_U = pi_1(U) and E_S = pi_1(S), with fundamental groups taken prime to the residual characteristics. For each section, with image the divisor L_i (called y_i(S) or Y(S) on the next page), the normalizer of the inertia at L_i maps onto E_S. This gives an extension (13): 1 -> T -> N(L_i) -> E_S -> 1, where T = lim mu_n = Zhat(1). Its class is c_i in H^2(E_S,T), which equals H^2(S,T) because S is a K(pi,1).

Kummer theory gives Pic(S)^ = Pic(S) tensor Zhat, injecting into H^2(S,T) (17).

This page:
(i) When S is of finite type over Q ('arithmetic case'), Pic(S) is a finitely generated Z-module (Mordell-Weil-Néron, i.e. Lang-Néron plus finite generation of Néron-Severi). Hence Pic(S) -> Pic(S)^ is injective, so the composite (18) Pic(S) -> H^2(S,T) is injective.
(ii) Main claim, in general: c_i lies in the image of (18). Precisely, c_i is the image of xi_i in Pic(S), the class of the conormal sheaf (or the normal sheaf, its dual; the sign is left open) of X along the section, i.e. J_i/J_i^2. So the inertia/decomposition extension at a cusp is classified by the l-adic (Zhat(1)) first Chern class of the (co)normal line bundle of the section.
(iii) Proof sketch: replace X by its formal completion along the section, a substitute for a tubular neighbourhood. Take the deleted (punctured) neighbourhood, viewed as a topos over S. Interpret (13) as the homotopy exact sequence of this punctured-neighbourhood topos over S, which is homotopically a 'circle bundle' with fibre a punctured formal disc whose pi_1 is Zhat(1). The class of such a circle fibration is the Euler/Chern class of the line bundle, as in topology (Gysin). The last lines are obscure; they seem to say the punctured neighbourhood is an 'ombre' (shadow) of a tubular neighbourhood that needs making precise.

The next page draws the consequence. In the arithmetic case (13) splits iff xi_i = 0, i.e. iff a global uniformizer along the section exists (a tangential base point). Splittings coming from trivializations of J/J^2 form a G_m(S)-torsor, while all splittings form a torsor under H^1(S,T), which equals G_m(S)^ in that case.
errors: The identification is stated with a sign/duality ambiguity (conormal vs normal); the correct class depends on orientation conventions for Zhat(1) and is not fixed on the page.

The 'proof' is only a principle: the étale homotopy type of the punctured formal neighbourhood as a topos over S, and its homotopy exact sequence, are not constructed. This is a real technical gap at the time, since formal completions are not schemes of finite type and purity/abhyankar-type arguments are needed.

The finite generation of Pic(S) needs S of finite type over Q (a finitely generated field); 'Mordell-Weil-Néron' covers Pic^0 of a compactification and Néron-Severi separately. Non-proper S is handled since Pic(S) is a quotient of Pic of a compactification. This is fine but implicit.

ideas.what: Class of the cuspidal decomposition/inertia extension 1->Zhat(1)->D->pi_1(S)->1 equals the Chern class of the (co)normal bundle of the section
ideas.modern_name: Euler class of the punctured tubular neighbourhood; obstruction to tangential base points / cuspidal sections in families
ideas.usually_credited_to: Topological analogue classical (Gysin, Euler class); arithmetic form implicit in work on tangential base points (Deligne 1989) and families of curves (Nakamura, Hain-Matsumoto, others)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Pic(S) -> H^2(S,Zhat(1)) injective for S of finite type over Q
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the l-adic cycle class on Pic via Lang-Néron + Néron-Severi finite generation
ideas.where_published: Related Kummer/Brauer discussion in Le groupe de Brauer I-III

ideas.what: Punctured formal neighbourhood of a section considered as a topos over S whose homotopy exact sequence realizes the decomposition-group extension
ideas.modern_name: Étale homotopy type of punctured tubular neighbourhoods / deleted formal neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later developments in étale homotopy and exit paths (unsure of precise attributions)

ideas.what: Splitting iff conormal bundle trivial, i.e. existence of a global uniformizer (next page)

missed.claim: A program to define the étale homotopy type of a punctured formal neighbourhood of a divisor as a topos fibred over S and derive the decomposition-group extension as its homotopy sequence, with Euler class = c_1 of the normal bundle. The page sketches this but does not carry it out.
missed.quote: on prend le complété formel de X le long de ... et on interprète la suite exacte (13) comme la suite exacte d'homotopie de ce topos ... au dessus de S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates étale tubular-neighbourhood / exit-path formalisms. It is a clean statement that the cuspidal extension class in H^2(pi_1(S),Zhat(1)) is the Chern class of the conormal bundle, which is useful for cuspidal sections in relative anabelian geometry. It is probably known to specialists, but rarely stated in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The result is the natural arithmetic analogue of the Euler-class description of a circle bundle and is folklore among specialists in tangential base points. Seeing Grothendieck state it explicitly, with the punctured-formal-neighbourhood-as-topos viewpoint and the link to global uniformizers, is a nice but not shocking unpublished detail.

'X la long de ξ' should read 'X le long de y_i(S)' (the section image), with element (19) ξ_i ∈ Pic(S)
'qui remplace - un voisinage ξ(S)' likely reads 'qui remplace un voisinage tubulaire de y_i(S)'
'[-groupe-] {+module+}' correction is consistent with the image: 'Z-module de type fini (par Mordell-Weil-Néron)'
